newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea steps in to support won vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea steps in to support won vs dlr.

text.p: The central bank of Korea intervened in the interbank market in early morning trading on Tuesday to support the falling won versus the dollar, dealers said.
But the bank denied the intervention, as it routinely does.
Dealers said the central bank started selling dollars when the won dropped to 844.90.
They said the market has been short on dollars as demand for the U.S. currency surged on the back of expected import deals and lack of year-end export negotiations.
The won is currently trading at 844.40.
